summary: Gone 1942 pole-tower lookout near Doty, Lewis County, WA; vandalized 1964; register and firelookout.com date removal 1966; remnants reported near summit.

facts.design: 28-foot pole tower with 7x7 ft cab and a house
facts.status_note: Vandalized in 1964. The register and firelookout.com date removal to 1966; a trip report says destroyed in 1964.

staffing.status: seasonal summer staffing; two women in summer 1954; run from Chehalis headquarters in fire season (1960 item)

access.note: On DNR land, about 5 miles of gravel roads, reached from a gate. The trip report says the roads have not had gates for many years but tells visitors to park at one. Inferred from an undated trip report that describes walking in; no closure notice seen.

visit.trail_note: About 0.8 mile hike from a gate, about 300 ft of gain. No tower remains. A 2015 landslide took out the road just past the gate.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1966. The trip report says destroyed in 1964. The June 1964 newspaper describes vandal damage but not removal. The story reports both dates and does not choose one.
The Weebly page quotes a July 30, 1954 item and a 1960 item putting Doty about 10 miles west of Chehalis. firelookout.com says 16 miles west. The story gives 10 and names firelookout.com's 16.

notes_for_editor: Removal date conflict: 1964 (trip report; the June 1964 newspaper describes damage, not removal) vs 1966 (register and firelookout.com). The Weebly 'Removed' heading has no date. Access level 'public' is inferred from DNR land and a walk-in described in an undated trip report (post-2015); that report also says the roads have not had gates for years but tells visitors to park at a gate, so check before going. The 1954 lookouts' names are omitted from the story. No WebSearch used; four cached pages read. Brief record checked: coordinates, elevation (634 m) and FFLOS registration match; no corrections. Fact-check 2026-10-09: firelookout.com's 16-mile figure is now in the story beside the 10-mile figure. 'Village of Doty' comes from the NGS description on the Weebly page; the cable theft comes from the June 19, 1964 item. The trip report's gate caveat is added to the access sentence.
